:::{#def-matrix-addition}
#### Matrix addition

Two matrices $\matr{A}$ and $\matr{B}$ of the same dimensions $m \times n$
can be added element-wise; their **matrix sum** is:

$$(\matr{A} + \matr{B})_{ij} = a_{ij} + b_{ij}$$

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-matrix-addition}
#### Adding matrices, and a sum that is not defined

$$
\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 \\ 3 & 4 \end{bmatrix}
+ \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 \end{bmatrix}
= \begin{bmatrix} 1 + 0 & 2 + 1 \\ 3 + 1 & 4 + 0 \end{bmatrix}
= \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 3 \\ 4 & 4 \end{bmatrix}.
$$

A $2 \times 2$ matrix and a $2 \times 3$ matrix cannot be added:
they do not have the same dimensions, so entry $(1, 3)$ of the sum would have no first term.

:::
